title: Small intestine
source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

main.t: The longest part of the digestive tract, where most digestion and practically all absorption take place.

simpler.t: Your small intestine is a long, coiled tube that takes the goodness from your food.

deeper.t: It is “small” only in diameter: about 2.5 cm, against 7.6 cm for the large intestine.

facts.t: It runs from the pyloric sphincter of the stomach to the caecum of the large intestine.
The jejunum and ileum hang from the posterior abdominal wall by the mesentery, framed by the large intestine.

simpler.t: It is coiled up in the middle of your abdomen, ringed by the large intestine.

deeper.t: The duodenum curves behind the peritoneum (retroperitoneal) round the head of the pancreas.

items.name: Duodenum
items.t: The shortest part, about 25 cm. It receives bile and pancreatic juice.

items.name: Jejunum
items.t: About 0.9 m in life. Its name means “empty”.

items.name: Ileum
items.t: The longest part, about 1.8 m. It joins the caecum at the ileocaecal valve.

items.name: Circular folds
items.t: Deep ridges of mucosa and submucosa that make chyme spiral and slow down.

items.name: Villi and microvilli
items.t: Finger-like projections and their tiny surface extensions, the brush border.

simpler.t: Three parts: duodenum, jejunum and ileum, lined with millions of tiny folds and fingers.
simpler.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). The number of villi (“millions”).

deeper.t: Circular folds, villi and microvilli increase its absorptive surface more than 600-fold.

facts.t: Each villus holds a capillary bed and a lacteal, so absorbed nutrients pass straight into blood or lymph.
Enzymes fixed to the microvilli finish digesting carbohydrates and proteins.
Segmentation mixes chyme with digestive juices and presses it against the mucosa.

simpler.t: A huge, finger-covered surface and churning movements help it absorb food.

items.name: Stomach
items.t: Releases chyme into the duodenum through the pyloric sphincter.

items.name: Bile duct and pancreatic duct
items.t: Join at the hepatopancreatic ampulla and open into the duodenum.

items.name: Large intestine (caecum)
items.t: Receives food residue from the ileum through the ileocaecal valve.

items.name: Hepatic portal vein
items.t: Carries nutrient-rich blood from it to the liver.

simpler.t: It starts at the stomach and ends at the large intestine, and its blood goes to the liver.

facts.t: It develops from the midgut of the embryo.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). The development of the small intestine.

facts.t: Peyer’s patches in the ileum are most prominent in young people and fade with age.
Some human populations keep making lactase as adults; in others, lactose intolerance is common.

items.injury: Too little lactase made by the absorptive cells.
items.damaged: Digestion of lactose, the milk sugar (lactose intolerance).
items.cannotDo: Eat dairy without gas, cramps, bloating and diarrhoea.
items.why: Bacteria in the large intestine ferment the undigested lactose, making gas.

items.damaged: The absorptive surface of the small intestine.
items.why: The surface area for absorption falls sharply.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). Conditions that flatten the villi and their effects.

items.q: Explain why the small intestine has such a large absorptive surface.
model: Circular folds make chyme spiral and slow down.
Villi cover the folds, about 20–40 per square millimetre.
Microvilli cover the cells of each villus.
Together they increase the surface more than 600-fold.

items.q: Compare the duodenum and the ileum.
model: Duodenum: shortest, about 25 cm, partly retroperitoneal.
It receives bile and pancreatic juice and has Brunner’s glands.
Ileum: longest, about 1.8 m, on the mesentery.
It has Peyer’s patches and ends at the ileocaecal valve.

items.q: Predict what happens in the colon of someone with lactose intolerance after drinking milk.
model: Lactose passes undigested through the small intestine.
Bacteria in the large intestine ferment it.

check.stem: Which is the longest part of the small intestine?
check.why: The ileum, about 1.8 m long, is the longest part.

options: A lymphatic capillary in a villus
check.why: Each villus contains a lymphatic capillary called a lacteal.

check.stem: Where do bile and pancreatic juice enter the small intestine?
check.why: Both reach the duodenum through the hepatopancreatic ampulla.
